mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes Vito 111-126 Petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Vito 111-126 Petrol engine replacement typically costs between £1,200 and £5,500 depending on engine code, condition type, and whether fitting is included. Rebuilt M111 (Vito 113 Petrol, W638): £1,500-£2,800 supply only. Rebuilt M112 (Vito 119/123 Petrol, W639): £2,000-£4,200 supply only. Rebuilt M272 (Vito 126 Petrol, W639): £2,800-£5,500 supply only. Used engines from breakers: £500-£2,800 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,200 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of M272 balance shaft failure in a Vito 126 Petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M272's balance shaft typically shows warning signs before complete failure. Rattling or clanking noise on cold start. Check engine light with cam/crank correlation codes (P0016/P0017/P0018/P0019). Loss of power and rough running. Metallic debris in engine oil. Most common on pre-2008 production M272 engines.

mainEntity.name: Is the M112 V6 engine in the Vito 119 and 123 Petrol reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M112 V6 is fundamentally a smooth and refined engine, but it has several well-documented weak points as mileage climbs. Head gasket degradation - composite gasket design prone to coolant-oil mixing. Oil leaks from camshaft plugs (30mm and 65mm) and rocker cover gaskets. Thermostat failure causing temperature fluctuations. With preventative maintenance, these engines can exceed 150,000-200,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my Vito 111-126 Petrol engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., timing chain tensioner on M111, head gaskets on M112, balance shaft on M272). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic timing failure. M111 timing chain tensioner: £250-£450 - do this at first sign of rattle. M112 head gasket replacement with MLS gaskets: £1,200-£1,800 - permanent fix. M272 balance shaft repair: £2,200-£3,500 - for pre-2008 engines. Full M111 rebuild: £1,500-£2,800 - for catastrophic failure or 150k+ miles. Full M112 rebuild: £2,200-£4,200 - for catastrophic failure or 120k+ miles. Full M272 rebuild: £2,800-£5,500 - for catastrophic failure or 120k+ miles. Given Vito 111-126 Petrol values (£2,000-£10,000), evaluate repair vs replacement carefully.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my Vito 111-126 Petrol has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block. W638 Vito 113 Petrol: M111.950 (2.0L, 129hp). W639 Vito 119 Petrol: M112.951 (3.2L, 218hp). W639 Vito 123 Petrol: M112.976 (3.7L, 231hp). W639 Vito 126 Petrol: M272.978 (3.5L, 258hp).

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used Vito 111-126 Petrol engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a Vito petrol. The W638 and W639 subframe geometry and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. Subframe must be lowered on W639 models - not a driveway job. V6 engine weight requires proper lifting equipment. ECU coding and immobiliser synchronisation required. Specialist supply & fit costs £800-£1,200 - worth every penny.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Vito 111-126 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes Vito 111-126 petrol range spans the W638 (1996-2003) and W639 (2003-2014) generations, powered by the M111 four-cylinder, M112 V6 and M272 V6 petrol engines. While rare in the UK market - petrol Vitos account for under 10% of sales - these smooth, refined units offered effortless power delivery for passenger variants and camper conversions at the cost of significant fuel consumption.

milestones.description: W638 Vito launched with M111 2.0L four-cylinder petrol, 129hp (95kW), transverse-mounted front-wheel-drive layout
W639 Vito launched with M112 3.2L V6 petrol, 218hp (160kW), longitudinal rear-wheel-drive layout
M112 3.7L V6 petrol introduced as a special-order option, 231hp (170kW)
M272 3.5L V6 petrol introduced in Vito 126, 258hp (190kW), replacing M112 in top-spec passenger variants
Petrol Vito production ends as W639 is replaced by W447 with predominantly diesel powertrains

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every petrol engine fitted to the Mercedes Vito 111-126 range is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points from real owner experience.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Vito 111-126 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Vito 111-126 petrol range relies on the M111 four-cylinder, M112 V6 and M272 V6 engine families - smooth and refined units that have developed well-documented reputations for predictable failures as mileages climb. Timing chain tensioner wear on the M111, head gasket degradation on the M112, and balance shaft failure on early M272 engines are the most frequently cited issues. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common Vito 111-126 petrol engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: M111 Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the Vito 113 Petrol Rattles on Start-Up
problems.rootCause: The M111's timing chain tensioner can lose oil pressure retention when parked, causing chain slack and a characteristic rattle on cold start. If left unaddressed, the chain can stretch and eventually skip teeth with catastrophic valve-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace hydraulic tensioner only, oil and filter change
repairOptions.longevity: 30k-40k miles; only viable if no chain damage yet

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles; corrects the root cause properly

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M111 with new timing components, upgraded tensioner
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required if chain has jumped

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W638 Vito 113 Petrol is worth £2,000-£5,000 depending on condition and mileage - the full replacement cost of £1,500-£2,800 often approaches vehicle value. For vehicles worth under £3,000, evaluate repair options carefully.
problems.recommendation: At the first sign of rattling on cold start, have the timing chain tensioner inspected immediately. The M111 is known as one of the strongest engines of its era, but ignoring chain rattle can lead to complete engine failure. On a high-mileage W638 Vito, a full rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is often the most cost-effective solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M111 Mercedes Vito 113 Petrol engine prices

problems.h4: M112 Head Gasket Failure - Why the Vito 119/123 Petrol Loses Coolant and Overheats
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Vito 119 Petrol, 123 Petrol (W639, 2003-2008, M112.951, M112.976)
problems.rootCause: The M112 V6 uses a composite head gasket design that is prone to degradation over time, particularly if the engine has been overheated. Coolant can leak into the oil galleries or oil into the cooling system, leading to overheating, loss of performance, and eventual engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace head gaskets with MLS (multi-layer steel) upgraded gaskets, pressure test heads, new bolts
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-150k miles; permanent fix with upgraded gaskets

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit reconditioned M112 with new head gaskets, timing components, and seals
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required if overheating has warped cylinder heads

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W639 Vito 119 or 123 Petrol is worth £3,000-£8,000 depending on condition and mileage - the full replacement cost of £2,200-£4,200 is modest relative to vehicle value for most examples. For vehicles worth under £4,000, evaluate repair options first.
problems.recommendation: If you notice coolant loss without an external leak, oil in the coolant, or white smoke from the exhaust, have the head gaskets inspected immediately. Specialist head gasket replacement with MLS upgraded gaskets is a permanent fix - use a specialist who has experience with M112 engines and can fit the updated MLS gaskets rather than OEM composite units.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M112 Mercedes Vito 119/123 Petrol engine prices

problems.h4: M112 Oil Leaks - Why the Vito V6 Petrol Drips Oil
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Vito 119 Petrol, 123 Petrol (W639, 2003-2008, M112.951, M112.976)
problems.rootCause: The M112 V6 is prone to oil leaks from multiple locations - camshaft plugs (30mm and 65mm), rocker cover gaskets, and oil cooler seals. These leaks are common on higher-mileage examples and can lead to oil loss, belt contamination, and eventual engine damage if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace rocker cover gaskets, new spark plug tube seals

repairOptions.tier: Camshaft Plug & Oil Cooler Seal Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace camshaft plugs (30mm and 65mm) and oil cooler seals
Supply & fit reconditioned M112 with new gaskets, seals, and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. For catastrophic failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a Vito 119 or 123 Petrol worth £3,000-£8,000, rocker cover gasket replacement at £250-£450 is excellent preventative maintenance. Full engine replacement is only justified for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the M112 are rarely urgent but should not be ignored - oil dripping onto the exhaust manifolds can create smoke and, in extreme cases, fire risk. The specialist camshaft plug and oil cooler seal replacement addresses the most common leak points in one go, saving on labour versus doing each repair individually.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M112 Mercedes Vito 119/123 Petrol engine prices

problems.h4: M272 Balance Shaft Failure - Why the Vito 126 Petrol Rattles and Loses Timing
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Vito 126 Petrol (W639, 2007-2014, M272.978 - early production engines only)
problems.rootCause: Early M272 engines (2004-2008 production) suffer from a balance shaft sprocket manufacturing defect where the sprocket teeth wear prematurely, causing the timing chain to slacken and camshaft timing to drift. Fault codes P0016/P0017/P0018/P0019 confirm the issue.

repairOptions.tier: Full Repair - Balance Shaft & Timing Components
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Engine-out replacement of balance shaft with updated hardened version, plus timing chain, guides, and tensioners
repairOptions.longevity: Permanent fix with updated parts; requires 20-30 labour hours

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of reconditioned M272 (post-2008 specification with hardened balance shaft)
repairOptions.longevity: The preferred option if engine has suffered valve damage or if vehicle has high mileage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W639 Vito 126 Petrol is worth £4,000-£10,000 depending on condition and mileage - the full replacement cost of £2,800-£5,500 is modest relative to vehicle value for most examples. For vehicles worth under £5,000, evaluate repair options carefully.
problems.recommendation: On a Vito 126 Petrol, balance shaft repair often approaches the vehicle's value. However, if the van is otherwise excellent, the updated balance shaft permanently resolves the issue. For high-mileage examples (120k+), replacement with a post-2008 rebuilt unit is often more cost-effective than repairing a worn engine. Check your engine number - not all M272 engines are affected.
